headline: Russia used the new 9M723-2 ballistic missile, known as the “Iskander-1000,” against Kyiv for the first time during one of the summer missile strikes, according to Ukraine’s Main Directorate of Intelligence (HUR). Ukraine claims that the missile is part of the “Bora-M” system and has a reported range of up to 550 km, although earlier reports claimed a range of up to 1,000 km. The increased range is reportedly achieved through a larger, more energy-dense solid-fuel motor, which also required modifications to the launcher. According to open-source claims, the missile may have a range of up to 1,000–1,300 km, with the additional propellant increasing the motor’s volume by around 10–15%. To accommodate the increased fuel capacity, the warhead is reportedly reduced to approximately 300–350 kg, compared with the standard 480 kg warhead of the Iskander-M. The missile is capable of carrying high-explosive fragmentation or cluster warheads and may feature enhanced maneuverability during the terminal phase, including evasive maneuvers at loads of approximately 20–30 g. It is also equipped or intended to be equipped with onboard electronic warfare systems and countermeasures such as chaff and thermal flares. The existence of an upgraded Iskander-M missile with a reported range of up to 1,000 km, hence its unofficial designation “Iskander-1000,” was first reported in July 2024. In December 2025, Ukrainian sources unofficially reported that the missile had already been used at a range of up to 800 km. In October 2025, Ukrainian sources published leaked Russian procurement documents indicating the planned production of 18 ballistic missiles under the designation 9M723-2. The missile is fitted with a combined guidance system, using inertial guidance during the initial and mid-course phases and an electro-optical/thermal-imaging seeker during the terminal phase. Its reported accuracy is claimed to be as high as 5 meters CEP.

headline: The U.S. Army has tested the M2A4 Bradley IFV as a carrier for FireAnt unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) mounted along its sides. The small FireAnt UGV weighs just 27 kg and can carry electronic warfare (EW) and electronic intelligence (ELINT) equipment, or be used as a kamikaze UGV. The long-term goal is for these drones to operate as part of a swarm. During the Pegasus Charge 3 exercise at Fort Hood, Texas, the FireAnt was demonstrated as a kamikaze UGV, intended to finish off vehicles disabled by small-arms fire. In theory, it could also be used against enemy fortifications or troops sheltering in bunkers while the Bradley provides suppressive fire. However, this concept raises some concerns in the context of the war in Ukraine. The FireAnts occupy the space normally used for the Bradley's side-mounted reactive armor, reducing the vehicle's protection. They also appear to require manual deployment by the crew or dismounted troops, which could be impractical during an active assault. Still, the idea of using existing combat vehicles to quickly deliver UGVs to the front line is interesting. It just needs further development and refinement.

headline: Ukraine carried out a large-scale, combined missile strike on Donetsk today, using a mix of FP-5 Flamingo cruise missiles, Storm Shadow/SCALP-EG cruise missiles, and potentially another unidentified munition. Two separate targets were struck. Six missiles hit an underground parking facility at an unfinished residential complex, while another seven struck an industrial building. Ukrainian channels claim both locations were being used to store large quantities of military equipment, including missile and rocket launchers, armored vehicles, and personnel. Several fragments with folded wings, typically associated with glide bombs and jet-powered stand-off munitions, were recovered. Based on the surviving markings, at least some of the munitions used in the strike have been identified as Storm Shadow/SCALP-EG cruise missiles. One fragment bears a manufacturer’s plate marked MBDA FRANCE, along with the manufacturer code F0555. Another fragment contains a toothed mechanism, serial number 10625, and the date 20.08.2024. This is likely part of the mechanism used to deploy or control the missile’s wing. As for the unidentified munition, one possibility is a weapon developed under the U.S. Extended-Range Attack Missile (ERAM) program. However, no confirmed photographs of an intact ERAM missile have emerged so far, making this identification highly speculative. Another possibility is the AGM-158A JASSM air-launched cruise missile.

headline: RT by @sentdefender:

The U.S. military is facing a major shortage of advanced air defense interceptors in Europe, particularly Patriot missiles, after large quantities of U.S. stocks were shifted to the Middle East during the war with Iran. A U.S. defense official in Europe told AP that American forces there do not have enough Patriots to defend against a sustained Russian ballistic missile attack and would have only limited capability against even a single such strike. A NATO official confirmed that Patriot inventories among U.S. and allied forces in Europe are low, although NATO disputes the characterization that the situation is “beyond critical.” The shortage has several causes. The U.S. transferred roughly 600 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine during the Biden administration, but the Iran war has accelerated consumption. CSIS estimates that about 1,500 of the U.S. inventory of roughly 2,330 Patriots have been expended during the Iran conflict. Europe has few immediate substitutes for Patriot against advanced ballistic missiles. France and Italy's SAMP/T provides another capability, but its current version has a shorter range and the newer SAMP/T NG has not yet been combat tested. Production is expected to improve, but not immediately. NATO expects Europe's first Patriot production facility, in Germany, to begin deliveries potentially in early 2027. U.S. production is also being expanded, with a goal of reaching 2,000 Patriot missiles annually by 2030. There is no indication that Russia is preparing an imminent attack on NATO, and Russia itself faces significant constraints from its ongoing war in Ukraine. However, the depleted inventories create a temporary vulnerability while the U.S. and European allies work to rebuild missile stocks. headline: The Pentagon is conducting a six month review of U.S. military deployments in Europe that will provide Secretary of War Pete Hegseth with at least four force posture options by Nov. 6, according to internal planning documents reviewed by Reuters. The options will assess different U.S. troop levels and locations, how quickly forces could be repositioned, and associated costs. The review covers roughly 80,000 U.S. personnel currently stationed in Europe. The review comes amid growing concern among European allies that the Trump administration could significantly reduce the U.S. military presence in Europe. Pentagon officials say the process is intended to develop a range of options, rather than a predetermined troop reduction. A key milestone will come by Sept. 18, when the top U.S. military commander in Europe is expected to participate in a briefing with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby to help shape the options ultimately presented to Hegseth. The review also comes as Washington has criticized some NATO members over their response to the Iran conflict, particularly regarding basing and overflight access for U.S. forces. The Pentagon has asked allies whether they are willing to reduce or eliminate restrictions on U.S. military access. Source: https://www.reuters.com/world/pentagons-nato-review-preparing-troop-options-hegseth-by-november-6-2026-08-27/

headline: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) Center has issued an advisory nearly 36 hours after receiving a report of a tanker struck by an unknown projectile, resulting in a fire aboard the vessel. According to UKMTO, all crew members are safe and accounted for, and no environmental impact has been reported. The incident appears to be separate from, and occurred earlier than, today's reported attack on a Kuwaiti tanker in the same general area. Attribution and the circumstances surrounding the earlier incident remain under investigation.
